subject: general
question: The average of five consecutive natural numbers is 12. What will be the average of the seven numbers if the next two natural numbers are also included?
solution:
Given:

The average of five consecutive natural numbers is 12.

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

Let the first natural number be N.

According to the question,

N + (N + 1) + (N + 2) + (N + 3) + (N + 4) = 12 × 5

⇒ 5N + 10 = 60

⇒ 5N = 50

⇒ N = 50/5

⇒ N = 10

Sum of the seven numbers

⇒ N + (N + 1) + (N + 2) + (N + 3) + (N + 4) + (N + 5) + (N + 6)

⇒ 7N + 21

⇒ 7 × 10 + 21

⇒ 91

Average of the seven numbers = 91/7 = 13

**∴ The average of the seven numbers if the next two natural numbers are also included will be 13.**
